+"""The token-chunked EP overlap path: parameters, TE grouped MLP, schedule.
+
+Compute is the caller's current stream; dispatch and combine share ONE comm stream.
+Chunk ``c``'s compute is left of the ``||``::
+
+    forward   (ascending)    FC1(c) -> FC2(c)   ||   Dispatch(c+1) or Combine(c-1)
+    backward  (descending)   dgrad(c)           ||   Dispatch(c-1) or Combine(c+1)
+                             wgrad(c)           ||   Combine(c)
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from collections.abc import Sequence
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from itertools import chain
+
+import torch
+from torch.autograd.function import once_differentiable
+
+from megatron.core.extensions.transformer_engine import TE_GROUPED_GEMM_EXPERT_TOKEN_ALIGNMENT
+from megatron.core.tensor_parallel.gtp_api import is_gtp_param
+
+# Aliased, not re-declared: a local 256 would silently size the chunk capacity against a
+# different alignment than the GEMM the schedule hands the chunk to.
+EXPERT_ALIGNMENT_TO_GROUPED_GEMM = TE_GROUPED_GEMM_EXPERT_TOKEN_ALIGNMENT
+
+
+def balanced_chunk_sizes(num_tokens: int, num_chunks: int) -> tuple[int, ...]:
+    """Split ``num_tokens`` into ``num_chunks`` sizes that differ by at most one."""
+    base, remainder = divmod(num_tokens, num_chunks)
+    return tuple(base + (1 if index < remainder else 0) for index in range(num_chunks))
+
+
+def chunk_offsets(chunk_sizes: tuple[int, ...]) -> tuple[int, ...]:
+    """Exclusive prefix sums of ``chunk_sizes``, with the total appended."""
+    offsets = [0]
+    for size in chunk_sizes:
+        offsets.append(offsets[-1] + size)
+    return tuple(offsets)
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class _MoEEPChunkOverlapConfig:
+    num_local_tokens: int
+    hidden_size: int
+    ffn_hidden_size: int
+    num_experts: int
+    router_topk: int
+    num_token_chunks: int
+    world_size: int
+    num_comm_SMs: int | None
+    #: Experts owned by THIS rank, supplied by the caller: world_size is the DISPATCH group
+    #: (ETP x EP), so num_experts // world_size would under-fetch weights and under-size capacity.
+    num_local_experts: int
+
+    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
+        if self.num_token_chunks < 1:
+            raise ValueError(f"num_token_chunks must be >= 1, got {self.num_token_chunks}")
+        if self.num_local_tokens < self.num_token_chunks:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"num_local_tokens ({self.num_local_tokens}) must be >= num_token_chunks "
+                f"({self.num_token_chunks}); an empty chunk is not a supported dispatch shape"
+            )
+
+    @property
+    def chunk_sizes(self) -> tuple[int, ...]:
+        """Token count of each of this rank's chunks."""
+        return balanced_chunk_sizes(self.num_local_tokens, self.num_token_chunks)
+
+    @property
+    def chunk_offsets(self) -> tuple[int, ...]:
+        """Row offset of each of this rank's chunks, with the total appended."""
+        return chunk_offsets(self.chunk_sizes)
+
+    @property
+    def largest_token_chunk_size(self) -> int:
+        """Rows in the largest chunk; every per-chunk buffer is sized for this one."""
+        return -(-self.num_local_tokens // self.num_token_chunks)
+
+    @property
+    def max_num_expanded_tokens_per_chunk(self) -> int:
+        """One chunk's receive capacity, rounded up to the grouped-GEMM alignment."""
+        num_local_experts = self.num_local_experts
+        rows = self.world_size * self.largest_token_chunk_size * min(
+            self.router_topk, num_local_experts
+        ) + num_local_experts * (EXPERT_ALIGNMENT_TO_GROUPED_GEMM - 1)
+        return -(-rows // EXPERT_ALIGNMENT_TO_GROUPED_GEMM) * EXPERT_ALIGNMENT_TO_GROUPED_GEMM
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class DispatchedChunk:
+    """One dispatch's receive, and the autograd node that produced it."""
+
+    recv_x: torch.Tensor
+    recv_probs: torch.Tensor
+    #: Alignment-padded received rows per LOCAL expert, straight from the dispatch manager.
+    split_sizes: torch.Tensor
+    #: ``(inputs, outputs)`` of the dispatch node. Differentiating it IS the combine adjoint,
+    #: so this path never spells one out: it is whatever the flex backend's own backward does.
+    graph: tuple[tuple[torch.Tensor, ...], tuple[torch.Tensor, ...]]
+
+
+@dataclass
+class CachedForwardChunkActivation:
+    """What one chunk's forward leaves behind for its backward."""
+
+    dispatched_tokens: torch.Tensor
+    routing_probs: torch.Tensor
+    fc2_output: torch.Tensor
+    #: The dispatch node, carried from the forward; see :class:`DispatchedChunk`.
+    dispatch_graph: tuple[tuple[torch.Tensor, ...], tuple[torch.Tensor, ...]]
+    #: ``(input, output)`` of the combine node, filled once the combine has run.
+    #: Differentiating it is the dispatch adjoint.
+    combine_graph: tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor] | None = None
+
+
+def ensure_expert_parameters_ready(experts: torch.nn.Module) -> None:
+    """Fire the expert linears' forward-pre hooks; skipping silently desyncs the DP all-gather."""
+    for submodule in chain(experts.linear_fc1.modules(), experts.linear_fc2.modules()):
+        for hook_id, hook in list(submodule._forward_pre_hooks.items()):
+            if hook_id in submodule._forward_pre_hooks_with_kwargs:
+                returned = hook(submodule, (), {})
+            else:
+                returned = hook(submodule, ())
+            if returned is not None:
+                raise RuntimeError(
+                    f"a {type(submodule).__name__} forward-pre hook returned a replacement "
+                    "input, which moe_ep_chunk_overlap cannot honour: it never calls forward"
+                )
+    experts._ensure_main_grad_for_fused_impl()
+
+
+def expert_weight_parameters(
+    experts: torch.nn.Module, num_local_experts: int
+) -> tuple[torch.nn.Parameter, ...]:
+    """Every expert ``weightN`` parameter, fc1's before fc2's."""
+    return tuple(
+        linear.get_parameter(f"weight{index}")
+        for linear in (experts.linear_fc1, experts.linear_fc2)
+        for index in range(num_local_experts)
+    )
+
+
+def check_fused_grouped_mlp(fc1_op, activation_op, fc2_op) -> None:
+    """Raise unless TE will fuse this triple and honour its recompute; both failures are silent."""
+    from transformer_engine.pytorch.ops.fused.grouped_mlp import (
+        GroupedMLP_CuTeGEMMGLU,
+        GroupedMLP_CuTeGEMMUnary,
+        ScaledSReLU,
+        _grouped_gemm_dsrelu_backward_supported,
+        _nvidia_cudnn_frontend_supports_wgrad,
+        is_glu_activation,
+        validate_grouped_mlp_dims,
+    )
+
+    fused = GroupedMLP_CuTeGEMMGLU if is_glu_activation(activation_op) else GroupedMLP_CuTeGEMMUnary
+    if not fused.is_supported():
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            f"TransformerEngine did not register {fused.__name__}, so this path would silently "
+            "run three unfused ops. TE before the split_alignment API also needs "
+            "NVTE_CUTEDSL_FUSED_GROUPED_MLP=1 exported BEFORE importing TE."
+        )
+
+    validate_grouped_mlp_dims(fc1_op, activation_op, fc2_op)
+
+    if activation_op.activation_recompute_in_mlp and not (
+        isinstance(activation_op, ScaledSReLU)
+        and _grouped_gemm_dsrelu_backward_supported()
+        and _nvidia_cudnn_frontend_supports_wgrad()
+    ):
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            "'moe_act' in recompute_modules asks TE for in-MLP recompute it will not do: "
+            f"op={type(activation_op).__name__} dsrelu={_grouped_gemm_dsrelu_backward_supported()}"
+            f" fe_wgrad={_nvidia_cudnn_frontend_supports_wgrad()}; TE saves the FC2 input anyway"
+        )
+
+
+def check_dispatch_capacity(payload: torch.Tensor, capacity: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Hold the dispatch width fixed: a varying one is what a CUDA-graph capture cannot serve."""
+    if payload.shape[0] != capacity:
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            f"a dispatch returned {payload.shape[0]} expanded rows, not the {capacity} the "
+            "expert GEMMs are compiled for: the pinned permuted-token count has drifted"
+        )
+    return payload
+
+
+def autocast_recipe() -> object:
+    """The quantization recipe of the live autocast; raises when no autocast surrounds it."""
+    from transformer_engine.pytorch.quantization import FP8GlobalStateManager
+
+    if not FP8GlobalStateManager.is_fp8_enabled():
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            "no live MXFP8 quantization autocast around this layer's forward. FIX: launch with "
+            "the mxfp8 recipe, or clear first_last_layers_bf16 (fp8_utils.py:714-724) here"
+        )
+    recipe = FP8GlobalStateManager.get_fp8_recipe()
+    if not recipe.mxfp8():
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            f"the live autocast carries a {type(recipe).__name__} recipe; this path implements "
+            "MXFP8 block scaling only, and going ahead would silently discard the configured one"
+        )
+    return recipe
+
+
+def _needs_backward_gather(shadow) -> bool:
+    from transformer_engine.pytorch.ops._common import is_quantized_tensor
+
+    if not is_quantized_tensor(shadow):
+        return False
+    return shadow._columnwise_data is None
+
+
+def _install_backward_gather(op, weights) -> int:
+    """Rematerialize an EGTP expert group COLUMNWISE for the backward."""
+    from transformer_engine.pytorch.cpu_offload import mark_not_offload
+
+    num_local_experts = len(weights)
+    shadows = [op.__dict__.get(f"weight{index}") for index in range(num_local_experts)]
+    stale = [i for i, s in enumerate(shadows) if s is not None and _needs_backward_gather(s)]
+    if not stale:
+        return 0
+
+    bwd_weights = list(weights[0].materialize_group_for_backward())
+
+    for index in stale:
+        shadow, bwd_w = shadows[index], bwd_weights[index]
+        columnwise_data = getattr(bwd_w, "_columnwise_data", None)
+        columnwise_scale = getattr(bwd_w, "_columnwise_scale_inv", None)
+
+        mark_not_offload(bwd_w)
+        shadow._columnwise_data = columnwise_data
+        shadow._columnwise_scale_inv = columnwise_scale
+
+        shadow._with_gemm_swizzled_scales = getattr(bwd_w, "_with_gemm_swizzled_scales", False)
+
+        shadow._rowwise_data = None
+        shadow._rowwise_scale_inv = None
+
+    op.__dict__["_egtp_bwd_weight_group"] = bwd_weights
+    return len(bwd_weights)
+
+
+def _attach_wgrad_accumulator(op, index: int, param) -> None:
+    """Give one EGTP expert's weight slot a full-sized ZEROED wgrad accumulator as ``main_grad``."""
+    accumulator = param.get_wgrad_tensor()
+    accumulator.zero_()
+    op.__dict__[f"weight{index}"].main_grad = accumulator
+
+
+def run_expert_forward(
+    runtime: MoEEPChunkOverlapRuntime, *, dispatched: DispatchedChunk, stream: torch.cuda.Stream
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, CachedForwardChunkActivation]:
+    """Run one chunk through the experts' OWN fused FC1 / activation / FC2."""
+    from transformer_engine.pytorch import autocast
+
+    runtime.expert_ops()
+    split_sizes = dispatched.split_sizes
+    dispatched_tokens = dispatched.recv_x.detach().requires_grad_(True)
+    routing_probs = dispatched.recv_probs.detach().reshape(-1).requires_grad_(True)
+
+    # The EXPERTS run the chunk, exactly as the trunk runs a whole microbatch: their
+    # `_fused_forward` owns the offload group, the padding decision and the op_kwargs.
+    with (
+        torch.cuda.stream(stream),
+        torch.enable_grad(),
+        autocast(enabled=True, recipe=autocast_recipe()),
+    ):
+        fc2_output, fc2_bias = runtime._experts(dispatched_tokens, split_sizes, routing_probs)
+        if fc2_bias is not None:
+            raise RuntimeError("moe_ep_chunk_overlap does not support an expert FC2 bias")
+        transport_output = fc2_output.detach()
+    return transport_output, CachedForwardChunkActivation(
+        dispatched_tokens=dispatched_tokens,
+        routing_probs=routing_probs,
+        fc2_output=fc2_output,
+        dispatch_graph=dispatched.graph,
+    )
+
+
+def run_expert_backward(
+    *, recv_x: torch.Tensor, saved: CachedForwardChunkActivation, stream: torch.cuda.Stream
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """Run the dgrad pair; the weight gradients stay parked for ``run_chunk_wgrad`` to drain."""
+
+    saved.dispatched_tokens.record_stream(stream)
+    saved.routing_probs.record_stream(stream)
+    saved.fc2_output.record_stream(stream)
+
+    with torch.cuda.stream(stream):
+        grad_input, grad_probs = torch.autograd.grad(
+            outputs=(saved.fc2_output,),
+            inputs=(saved.dispatched_tokens, saved.routing_probs),
+            grad_outputs=(recv_x,),
+            retain_graph=False,
+        )
+    return grad_input, grad_probs
+
+
+class _MoEEPChunkOverlapFunction(torch.autograd.Function):
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def forward(
+        ctx,
+        hidden_states: torch.Tensor,
+        routing_map: torch.Tensor,
+        dense_probs: torch.Tensor,
+        runtime: "MoEEPChunkOverlapRuntime",
+        *expert_weights: torch.Tensor,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        """Run the chunked forward, saving each chunk's activation for the backward."""
+        output, saved_fwd = runtime.moe_forward(hidden_states, routing_map, dense_probs)
+        ctx.runtime = runtime
+        ctx.saved_fwd = saved_fwd
+        ctx.num_expert_weights = len(expert_weights)
+
+        ctx.set_materialize_grads(False)
+        return output
+
+    @staticmethod
+    @once_differentiable
+    def backward(ctx, grad_output: torch.Tensor | None):
+        """Run the chunked backward, returning grads for the inputs and expert weights."""
+        runtime = ctx.runtime
+        saved_fwd = ctx.saved_fwd
+
+        ctx.runtime = None
+        ctx.saved_fwd = None
+
+        grad_hidden_states, grad_dense_probs, wgrad_placeholders = runtime.moe_backward(
+            saved_fwd, grad_output
+        )
+        return (grad_hidden_states, None, grad_dense_probs, None) + wgrad_placeholders
+
+
+class MoEEPChunkOverlapRuntime:
+    """One layer's transport, compiled GEMMs and borrowed expert parameters."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        *,
+        num_experts: int,
+        router_topk: int,
+        hidden_size: int,
+        ffn_hidden_size: int,
+        num_chunks: int,
+        num_comm_SMs: int | None,
+        experts: torch.nn.Module,
+        tp_ep_group: torch.distributed.ProcessGroup,
+        num_local_experts: int,
+        managers: Sequence[object],
+    ) -> None:
+        if tp_ep_group is None:
+            raise ValueError("moe_ep_chunk_overlap requires pg_collection.tp_ep, but it is None")
+

+def _expert_math(hidden, topk_indices, topk_weights, fc1_weight, fc2_weight):
+    """Weighted squared-ReLU MoE in FP32: ``sum_k w[t,k] * fc2(srelu(fc1(x[t])))``.
+
+    Row-independent by construction, so chunking it must be exact up to FP32 associativity in the
+    weight-gradient reduction.
+    """
+    preactivation = torch.einsum("th,tkih->tki", hidden, fc1_weight[topk_indices])
+    activation = torch.relu(preactivation) ** 2
+    expert_output = torch.einsum("tki,tkhi->tkh", activation, fc2_weight[topk_indices])
+    return (expert_output * topk_weights.unsqueeze(-1)).sum(dim=1)
+

+class _FakeDispatchManager:
+    """One chunk's collectives, as the identity plus the padding the schedule insists on.
+
+    The schedule holds every dispatch at ``max_num_expanded_tokens_per_chunk`` and
+    ``check_dispatch_capacity`` raises otherwise, so an identity leg would not even run: this
+    one pads to capacity and takes the padding back in the combine. Both legs are ordinary
+    differentiable ops, which is the point -- the schedule gets its adjoints by differentiating
+    the nodes these build, so a fake that returned a detached tensor would make the backward
+    this file exists to test unrunnable.
+
+    What it does NOT do is permute into expert-major order. The production manager does; what
+    is on trial here is the chunking and the custom backward, and a permutation would only
+    make the one-shot reference harder to write without covering anything new.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        #: Set by `_ensure_built`, which is where the geometry is first known.
+        self.capacity: int | None = None
+        self._live_rows: int | None = None
+        self.dispatched_probs: torch.Tensor | None = None
+        #: The schedule pins this before every dispatch; production reads it to skip a host
+        #: sync. Nothing here needs it, but it must be assignable or the schedule would fail.
+        self.num_permuted_tokens: int | None = None
+
+    def setup_metadata(self, routing_map, probs, padding_mask=None):
+        """Take this chunk's routing, exactly as the trunk manager is handed it."""
+        self._routing_map = routing_map
+        self._probs = probs
+
+    def dispatch(self, hidden_states):
+        self._live_rows = hidden_states.shape[0]
+        self.dispatched_probs = self._pad(self._probs)
+        return self._pad(hidden_states)
+
+    def combine(self, hidden_states):
+        return hidden_states[: self._live_rows]
+
+    def get_number_of_tokens_per_expert(self):
+        """Per-LOCAL-expert receive counts, summing to the live rows, with no permutation to
+        describe: one expert nominally owns them all."""
+        counts = torch.zeros(_NUM_EXPERTS, dtype=torch.long, device=self._probs.device)
+        counts[0] = self._live_rows
+        return counts
+
+    def _pad(self, tensor):
+        """Zero-pad to capacity. ``torch.cat`` so the padding is part of the graph: its backward
+        is the slice that drops those rows' gradients, which is what the real combine does."""
+        rows = self.capacity - tensor.shape[0]
+        return torch.cat([tensor, tensor.new_zeros((rows, *tensor.shape[1:]))], dim=0)
+
+
+def _routing_map_of(dense_probs: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """The boolean map the router hands the layer: true exactly where a probability is live."""
+    return dense_probs.detach() != 0
+

+class _AutogradRuntime(MoEEPChunkOverlapRuntime):
+    """The real runtime with its native compute replaced by autograd over the same expert math.
+
+    Only the build step and the per-chunk stages are overridden, so the two-stream schedule, the
+    generation lifecycle, the chunking and the autograd node under test are production code; the
+    collectives become `_FakeDispatchManager`'s pad-and-unpad, leaving the stream and event
+    plumbing running for real over compute autograd can differentiate. Its wgrad methods simply
+    OVERRIDE the runtime's own, so the schedule's ``self.<stage>()`` reaches this class by
+    ordinary inheritance.
+    """
+
+    fc1_weight: torch.Tensor
+    fc2_weight: torch.Tensor
+    #: The wgrad stage in call order, produced by the real ``moe_backward``. Bound by
+    #: `_make_facade` so the publish probe appends to the same list this fake does.
+    wgrad_log: list
+
+    def _ensure_built(self, flat_hidden):
+        # Phase TWO only: the inherited __init__ is the keyword surface, so a renamed keyword
+        # raises there. No super() -- it reads `weight{i}` and makes a real comm stream.
+        if self.comm_stream is not None:
+            return
+        self.config = ep_chunk_overlap._MoEEPChunkOverlapConfig(
+            num_local_tokens=flat_hidden.shape[0],
+            hidden_size=self._hidden_size,
+            ffn_hidden_size=self._ffn_hidden_size,
+            num_experts=self._num_experts,
+            router_topk=self._router_topk,
+            num_token_chunks=self._num_chunks,
+            world_size=torch.distributed.get_world_size(self._tp_ep_group),
+            num_comm_SMs=self._num_comm_SMs,
+            num_local_experts=self._num_local_experts,
+        )
+        self.device = torch.device(flat_hidden.device)
+        self.comm_stream = torch.cuda.Stream(device=self.device)
+        # The managers were built by `_build_facade` and validated by the inherited __init__;
+        # only the capacity is new here, because the geometry is what this phase resolves.
+        for manager in self._managers:
+            manager.capacity = self.config.max_num_expanded_tokens_per_chunk
+        # Dropped, not left at the constructor's None: both compute stages are overridden, so an
+        # accidental `expert_ops()` must be an AttributeError, not a real `build_expert_ops`.
+        del self._ops, self._fc1_op, self._fc2_op
+
+        # The Function's weight inputs, cached at build time as the production runtime does.
+        # These are not a `TEGroupedMLP`'s `weight{i}` parameters, which is why the fake has them.
+        self.expert_params = (self.fc1_weight, self.fc2_weight)
+
+        self.fc1_main_grad = torch.zeros_like(self.fc1_weight)
+        self.fc2_main_grad = torch.zeros_like(self.fc2_weight)
+        # Mirrors TE's per-op WeightGradStore: a FIFO with no chunk identity, which the schedule
+        # must drain exactly one entry from per chunk.
+        self._wgrad_queue: list = []
+        #: One entry per chunk: the offload gate the runtime threaded down to that chunk's compute.
+        self.offload_log: list = []
+
+    def begin_wgrad_accumulation(self):
+        """Nothing to ready: this fake accumulates into buffers its own build allocated."""
+        self.wgrad_log.append("begin")
+
+    def end_wgrad_accumulation(self):
+        """The EGTP flush leg; this fake owns no GTP group, so only its POSITION is asserted.
+
+        It must land after every chunk's drain (or the staging buffers hold a partial sum) and
+        after the publish (or DDP's post hook adds a stale ``param.grad`` into ``main_grad``:
+        ``zero_grad_buffer`` clears only the flag -- distributed_data_parallel.py:575-578, :699).
+        """
+        self.wgrad_log.append("flush")
+
+    def routed_experts_compute_forward(self, dispatched):
+        # The gate no longer rides this call: the experts' own fused forward owns the group, so
+        # the fake reads the flag off the experts module, which is where production reads it.
+        self.offload_log.append(self._experts.offload_fused_group_mlp)
+        # The WHOLE capacity window, as the real compute takes it: its dX must come back at
+        # capacity. Padded rows carry zero probabilities, so they contribute and take nothing.
+        hidden = dispatched.recv_x.detach().float().requires_grad_(True)
+        probs = dispatched.recv_probs.detach().float().requires_grad_(True)
+        with torch.enable_grad():
+            # Top-k off the DENSE row, which is the form the schedule now dispatches; the
+            # one-shot reference takes the same two lines, so the two stay comparable.
+            weights, indices = torch.topk(probs, k=self._router_topk, dim=-1, sorted=True)
+            output = _expert_math(hidden, indices, weights, self.fc1_weight, self.fc2_weight)
+        # The saved chunk carries this fake's own inner graph in the same three slots the real
+        # one carries TE's, plus the dispatch NODE, which only the schedule differentiates.
+        saved = CachedForwardChunkActivation(
+            dispatched_tokens=hidden,
+            routing_probs=probs,
+            fc2_output=output,
+            dispatch_graph=dispatched.graph,
+        )
+        return output.detach().to(dispatched.recv_x.dtype), saved
+
+    def routed_experts_compute_backward(self, saved, grad_recv):
+        inputs = [saved.dispatched_tokens, saved.routing_probs, self.fc1_weight, self.fc2_weight]
+        grad_hidden, grad_probs, grad_fc1, grad_fc2 = torch.autograd.grad(
+            saved.fc2_output, inputs, grad_recv.float()
+        )
+        # Parked rather than returned, exactly as TE parks a deferred wgrad: the weight gradients
+        # stay the wgrad stage's work and never cross the seam.
+        self._wgrad_queue.append((grad_fc1, grad_fc2))
+        # Flat, as the production stage returns it; the schedule views it back onto the
+        # dispatch node's own probability output.
+        return grad_hidden.to(grad_recv.dtype), grad_probs.reshape(-1)
+
+    def run_chunk_wgrad(self, *, stream):
+        """Wgrad leg. The stream is checked here now that the schedule supplies it directly."""
+        # `==` not `is`: torch.cuda.current_stream() builds a fresh wrapper per call, so identity
+        # fails even for the same underlying cudaStream_t, which __eq__ compares.
+        assert stream == torch.cuda.current_stream(self.device), (
+            "the wgrad drain is handed the compute stream, never asks for one; the schedule passes "
+            f"the same stream its events are recorded on, got {stream}"
+        )
+        self.wgrad_log.append("chunk")
+        assert len(self._wgrad_queue) == 1, (
+            f"the deferred wgrad queue holds {len(self._wgrad_queue)} entries at the drain point, "
+            "not exactly one; this chunk's wgrad is missing or belongs to another chunk"
+        )
+        grad_fc1, grad_fc2 = self._wgrad_queue.pop()
+        # Straight into main_grad, as TE's `backward_dw` accumulates: nothing is held back for a
+        # later publish, because publishing no longer moves gradients -- it hands DDP placeholders.
+        self.fc1_main_grad += grad_fc1
+        self.fc2_main_grad += grad_fc2
+

+class _StubOverlap:
+    """Stand-in facade that records its calls and keeps its inputs in the autograd graph."""
+
+    def __init__(self):
+        self.calls = []
+
+    def forward(self, hidden_states, dense_probs, routing_map):
+        self.calls.append((hidden_states, dense_probs, routing_map))
+        flat = hidden_states.reshape(-1, hidden_states.shape[-1])
+        scale = dense_probs.sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True).to(flat.dtype)
+        return (flat * scale).view(hidden_states.shape), None
+

+def _install_publish_probe(monkeypatch, published: list, wgrad_log: list | None = None) -> None:
+    """Shadow the one TransformerEngine symbol ``moe_backward`` imports for itself.
+
+    ``publish_wgrad`` was inlined, so this is the only seam left at which the publish can be
+    observed, and the only real TE touch on either fake's path. Each call's parameters are
+    appended to ``published`` in call order.
+    """
+
+    def get_dummy_wgrads_for_params(params):
+        params = list(params)
+        if wgrad_log is not None:
+            wgrad_log.append("publish")
+        published.append(tuple(params))
+        # ``None`` where TE returns a real placeholder: autograd accepts it for an input that
+        # takes no gradient, and these two tensors are not DDP-managed parameters.
+        return [None] * len(params)
+
+    common = ModuleType("transformer_engine.pytorch.ops._common")
+    common.get_dummy_wgrads_for_params = get_dummy_wgrads_for_params
+    monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules, "transformer_engine.pytorch.ops._common", common)

+def _patch_schedule_stages(monkeypatch) -> None:
+    """Replace the five schedule stages both fakes below stand in for.
+
+    By NAME, so a rename raises here -- the rename detector as well as the substitution.
+    ``ensure_expert_parameters_ready`` is a module function; the other four are METHODS, patched
+    on the class, where each is bound at call time and the runtime arrives as ``self`` -- exactly
+    what the module functions were handed as ``runtime``. The three wgrad entries are
+    ``_AutogradRuntime``'s own overrides, which already win by MRO, so patching the base class
+    changes no behaviour and keeps the detector.
+    """
+    monkeypatch.setattr(ep_chunk_overlap, "ensure_expert_parameters_ready", lambda experts: None)
+    for name, replacement in (
+        ("quantize_expert_weights", lambda runtime: None),
+        ("begin_wgrad_accumulation", _AutogradRuntime.begin_wgrad_accumulation),
+        ("run_chunk_wgrad", _AutogradRuntime.run_chunk_wgrad),
+        ("end_wgrad_accumulation", _AutogradRuntime.end_wgrad_accumulation),
+    ):
+        monkeypatch.setattr(MoEEPChunkOverlapRuntime, name, replacement)
+
+
+def _build_facade(*, hidden_size, ffn_hidden_size, num_chunks, offload) -> MoEEPChunkOverlapRuntime:
+    """Whatever runtime class is currently patched into the package, built as production does."""
+    # The one field the runtime reads off `experts` itself: its activation-offload gate, read by
+    # NAME, so a rename on the trunk's side is an AttributeError in every test here.
+    experts = torch.nn.Identity()
+    experts.offload_fused_group_mlp = offload
+    # Resolved through the package, not through the name imported above: that attribute is the
+    # switch `_make_facade` flips to put a fake runtime class in production's place.
+    return overlap_module.MoEEPChunkOverlapRuntime(
+        num_experts=_NUM_EXPERTS,
+        router_topk=_ROUTER_TOPK,
+        hidden_size=hidden_size,
+        ffn_hidden_size=ffn_hidden_size,
+        num_chunks=num_chunks,
+        num_comm_SMs=_NUM_COMM_SMS,
+        experts=experts,
+        tp_ep_group=get_default_pg_collection().tp_ep,
+        num_local_experts=_NUM_EXPERTS,
+        # ONE PER CHUNK, as `moe_layer.py` builds them; the inherited __init__ refuses any
+        # other count.
+        managers=[_FakeDispatchManager() for _ in range(num_chunks)],
+    )
+
+
+def _make_inputs(generator, device, hidden_shape, num_tokens):
+    """Hidden states plus the sparse dense row the router produces: only top-k is non-zero."""
+    hidden = (
+        torch.randn(hidden_shape, generator=generator, device=device, dtype=torch.float32)
+        .mul_(0.5)
+        .to(torch.bfloat16)
+        .requires_grad_(True)
+    )
+    logits = torch.randn(
+        (num_tokens, _NUM_EXPERTS), generator=generator, device=device, dtype=torch.float32
+    )
+    top_values, top_indices = torch.topk(logits.softmax(dim=-1), k=_ROUTER_TOPK, dim=-1)
+    dense_probs = torch.zeros_like(logits).scatter(1, top_indices, top_values)
+    return hidden, dense_probs.requires_grad_(True)
+
+
+def _make_layer(config: TransformerConfig) -> MoELayer:
+    submodules = get_submodules(
+        get_gpt_layer_local_submodules(num_experts=_NUM_EXPERTS, moe_grouped_gemm=False).mlp
+    )
+    assert isinstance(submodules, MoESubmodules)
+    return MoELayer(config, submodules).cuda()
+
+
+def _spy_on_dispatcher(monkeypatch, layer: MoELayer) -> list[str]:
+    """Record every token-dispatcher phase method the layer invokes, in call order."""
+    called: list[str] = []
+    dispatcher = layer.token_dispatcher
+    for method_name in _DISPATCHER_METHODS:
+        original = getattr(dispatcher, method_name)
+
+        def make_spy(name, func):
+            def spy(*args, **kwargs):
+                called.append(name)
+                return func(*args, **kwargs)
+
+            return spy
+
+        monkeypatch.setattr(dispatcher, method_name, make_spy(method_name, original))
+    return called
+

+class TestSplitExecutionMap:
+    """The three-phase split that partial CUDA graphs drive must equal the single call.
+
+    ``MoETransformerLayer._forward_mlp_{router,expert_compute,postprocess}`` rewrite
+    ``fwd_execution_map`` and thread ``intermediate_tensors`` between three separate
+    ``MoELayer.forward`` calls, capturing the first and last. The overlap path used to refuse
+    that outright; these assert the refusal was conservative rather than necessary, by driving
+    the split by hand -- no graph capture, so a failure here is the SPLIT, not the capture.
+    """
+
+    def setup_method(self, method):
+        Utils.initialize_model_parallel(1, 1)
+        _set_random_seed(seed_=123, data_parallel_random_init=False)
+
+    def teardown_method(self, method):
+        Utils.destroy_model_parallel()
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _layer_with_stub_runtime():
+        """A real MoELayer whose routed-expert region is a deterministic stand-in.
+
+        The runtime is stubbed, not the layer: what is under test is ``custom_forward``'s
+        phase plumbing, and a real transport would add EP collectives this test does not need.
+        """
+        layer = _make_grouped_layer(_make_config(moe_ep_chunk_overlap=True, moe_grouped_gemm=True))
+        assert layer.moe_ep_chunk_overlap is not None, "the overlap path must be the active one"
+
+        class _StubRuntime:
+            calls = 0
+
+            def forward(self, hidden_states, probs, routing_map):
+                """Deterministic in both inputs, so a dropped or reordered phase shows up.
+
+                Shape contract copied from the real runtime: it flattens to [tokens, hidden]
+                and returns ``flat_output.view(input_shape), None``. The routing map arrives
+                as the third argument because ``preprocess`` stashes it for the expert phase,
+                which under 1F1B is a separate callable that is handed nothing else.
+                """
+                type(self).calls += 1
+                flat = hidden_states.reshape(-1, hidden_states.shape[-1])
+                out = flat * 2.0 + probs.sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
+                return out.view(hidden_states.shape), None
+
+        layer.moe_ep_chunk_overlap = _StubRuntime()
+        return layer
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _input(layer):
+        generator = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(11)
+        return torch.randn(
+            (_SEQUENCE_LENGTH, _MICRO_BATCH_SIZE, _HIDDEN_SIZE),
+            generator=generator,
+            device="cuda",
+            dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+        )
+
+    def test_split_execution_equals_the_single_call(self):
+        """The headline: three phases threaded by intermediate_tensors == one unsplit call."""
+        layer = self._layer_with_stub_runtime()
+        hidden_states = self._input(layer)
+
+        layer.fwd_execution_map = ["route", "expert_compute", "postprocess"]
+        whole, whole_bias = layer(hidden_states)
+
+        layer.fwd_execution_map = "route"
+        routed, probs, shared = layer(hidden_states, intermediate_tensors=())
+        layer.fwd_execution_map = "expert_compute"
+        expert_out, split_bias = layer(None, intermediate_tensors=(routed, probs))
+        layer.fwd_execution_map = "postprocess"
+        split = layer(None, intermediate_tensors=(expert_out, shared))
+
+        assert split.shape == whole.shape
+        assert torch.equal(
+            split, whole
+        ), f"split != whole: {int(torch.ne(split, whole).sum())}/{whole.numel()} differ"
+        assert split_bias == whole_bias
+
+    def test_the_split_really_went_through_the_overlap_runtime(self):
+        """Guards the test itself: a stub that never fired would make the above vacuous."""
+        layer = self._layer_with_stub_runtime()
+        hidden_states = self._input(layer)
+        before = type(layer.moe_ep_chunk_overlap).calls
+
+        layer.fwd_execution_map = "route"
+        routed, probs, _shared = layer(hidden_states, intermediate_tensors=())
+        layer.fwd_execution_map = "expert_compute"
+        layer(None, intermediate_tensors=(routed, probs))
+
+        assert type(layer.moe_ep_chunk_overlap).calls == before + 1
+
+    def test_padding_mask_is_still_refused(self):
+        """The one per-forward refusal that was NOT conservative: it stays."""
+        layer = self._layer_with_stub_runtime()
+        hidden_states = self._input(layer)

+        with pytest.raises(NotImplementedError, match="padding_mask"):
+            layer(hidden_states, padding_mask=mask)

+        # offloadable, so it reads 0 at num_chunks=1 where the single group is marked resident.
+        self.offload_bytes = 0

+        self.references: dict[int, torch.Tensor] = {}

+    comparison would only test a timing race that a clean run proves nothing about."""
+    probe = _OffloadProbe()
+    original_reload = ChunkOffloadHandler.reload

+    def offload(handler, src_tensor, pin_memory=True, use_cpu_pool=True):

+        # branch has a free-before-H2D of its own that this path must never reach.

+        torch.cuda._sleep(int(2e7))

+        # `view_meta` before comparing anything -- SILENTLY. None: contiguous() bars alias views.
+        return (src_tensor.device, cpu_backup, use_cpu_pool, None)

+    def reload(handler, state, non_blocking=None):

+            # races its own D2H stays observable here instead of being synchronized away.

+                    f"reloaded tensor {tuple(tensor.shape)} differs from the offloaded source"
+                )

+    monkeypatch.setattr(ChunkOffloadHandler, "reload", reload)
+    return probe

+class _DuckTypedExperts(torch.nn.Module):
+    """Everything the package READS off ``experts``, on a module that is not a ``TEGroupedMLP``.
+
+    The package builds no TransformerEngine ops of its own any more: it BORROWS the experts' own
+    sequence and CALLS the experts' own forward. So this stand-in has to be callable and has to
+    carry ``_fused_ops`` / ``_make_fused_ops``, and the construction below mirrors
+    ``TEGroupedMLP._make_fused_ops`` (experts.py:548-720) -- TE's and the trunk's behaviour, not
+    the package's. That construction moving in here is a real cost: nothing in this file now
+    pins WHICH activation op the production path picks, only that it checks whatever it got.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, *, gated: bool = False, activation_recompute: bool = False) -> None:
+        # `torch.nn.Module.__init__`, never `super()`: `_FakeExperts` below mixes this with
+        # `TEGroupedMLP`, whose own __init__ takes a config, a module spec and TransformerEngine.
+        torch.nn.Module.__init__(self)
+        # FC1 carries gate and up when gated, as ``TEGroupedMLP`` builds it (experts.py:218-221).
+        fc1_out = 2 * _FFN_HIDDEN_SIZE if gated else _FFN_HIDDEN_SIZE
+        self.linear_fc1 = _FakeGroupedLinear(fc1_out, _HIDDEN_SIZE)
+        self.linear_fc2 = _FakeGroupedLinear(_HIDDEN_SIZE, _FFN_HIDDEN_SIZE)
+        # The trunk's own 'moe_act' predicate, derived on the experts (experts.py:275-278) and
+        # read back by ``_make_fused_ops`` at experts.py:637.
+        self.activation_recompute = activation_recompute
+        self.config = SimpleNamespace(
+            activation_func=F.silu if gated else squared_relu,
+            gated_linear_unit=gated,
+            activation_func_clamp_value=None,
+            moe_mlp_glu_interleave_size=None,
+        )
+        # In a TUPLE and None until the first build, exactly as experts.py:351 leaves it: a bare
+        # module here registers the op shells as submodules and doubles every expert parameter.
+        self._fused_ops: tuple | None = None
+        #: One entry per ``_make_fused_ops`` call, so a second shell is counted, not inferred.
+        self.make_fused_ops_calls = 0
+        #: What the package asked the builder for, so the two overrides can be asserted on.
+        self.fused_ops_overrides: tuple | None = None
+        #: Per ``forward``: ``(hidden, tokens_per_expert, probs, the sequence already existed)``.
+        self.forward_calls: list = []
+        #: ``forward``'s second return value; a non-None one is what the seam has to refuse.
+        self.fc2_bias: torch.Tensor | None = None
+
+    def _make_activation_op(self, te_ops) -> torch.nn.Module:
+        """The activation ``TEGroupedMLP`` picks for this config (experts.py:637-708)."""
+        recompute = {"activation_recompute_in_mlp": self.activation_recompute}
+        if self.config.gated_linear_unit and self.config.activation_func is F.silu:
+            return te_ops.ScaledSwiGLU(
+                glu_interleave_size=self.config.moe_mlp_glu_interleave_size, **recompute
+            )
+        if not self.config.gated_linear_unit and self.config.activation_func is squared_relu:
+            return te_ops.ScaledSReLU(**recompute)
+        raise RuntimeError("_make_fused_ops expected SwiGLU, quick_gelu, or weighted squared_relu")
+
+    def make_fused_ops(
+        self, *, delay_wgrad_compute=None, accumulate_into_main_grad=None
+    ) -> torch.nn.Module:
+        """``TEGroupedMLP``'s public builder, which is the seam the package borrows through.
+
+        The overrides are recorded rather than applied: what the package must prove is that it
+        asks for both, since neither global config flag is required of the model any more.
+        """
+        self.fused_ops_overrides = (delay_wgrad_compute, accumulate_into_main_grad)
+        return self._make_fused_ops()
+
+    def _make_fused_ops(self) -> torch.nn.Module:
+        """TE's FC1/activation/FC2 container, carrying the experts' REAL weight parameters.
+
+        ``register_grouped_linear_params`` (experts.py:554-573) puts each linear's own
+        ``weight{i}`` onto the meta op shell, which is what makes a shadow written into that
+        shell's ``__dict__`` hide a live parameter rather than a copy of one.
+        """
+        from transformer_engine.pytorch import ops as te_ops
+
+        self.make_fused_ops_calls += 1
+        linear_ops = []
+        for linear in (self.linear_fc1, self.linear_fc2):
+            weights = [linear.get_parameter(f"weight{i}") for i in range(linear.num_gemms)]
+            op = te_ops.GroupedLinear(
+                linear.num_gemms,
+                linear.in_features,
+                linear.out_features,
+                bias=False,
+                device="meta",
+                dtype=weights[0].dtype,
+                accumulate_into_main_grad=True,
+                delay_wgrad_compute=True,
+            )
+            for index, weight in enumerate(weights):
+                op.register_parameter(f"weight{index}", weight)
+            linear_ops.append(op)
+        return te_ops.Sequential(linear_ops[0], self._make_activation_op(te_ops), linear_ops[1])
+
+    def forward(self, hidden_states, tokens_per_expert, permuted_probs):
+        """``TEGroupedMLP.forward``'s shape: record the call, return ``(output, bias)``."""
+        self.forward_calls.append(
+            (hidden_states, tokens_per_expert, permuted_probs, self._fused_ops is not None)
+        )
+        output = torch.zeros((hidden_states.shape[0], _HIDDEN_SIZE), requires_grad=True)
+        return output, self.fc2_bias
+
+    #: ``TEGroupedMLP`` resolves this at construction; the schedule refuses to borrow unless it
+    #: is True, because the unfused forward defers no weight gradient for it to drain.
+    _with_fused_impl = True
+
+    def _ensure_main_grad_for_fused_impl(self) -> None:
+        """``TEGroupedMLP``'s own lazy ``main_grad`` hook, fired through the seam."""
+
+

+#: An unrequested usage is present-and-``None``, never absent: that is how the boundary decides.
+_MXFP8_INNER = ("_rowwise_data", "_columnwise_data", "_rowwise_scale_inv", "_columnwise_scale_inv")

+class _StubQuantizedTensor(torch.Tensor):
+    """What a TE quantizer returns: a tensor, and deliberately NOT a Parameter, so the offload
+    hooks would manage it unless the package marks it.
+
+    Carries MXFP8's four inner slots, because the ONE thing TE's fused dgrad reads off a saved
+    weight is ``_columnwise_data`` / ``_columnwise_scale_inv`` (``grouped_mlp.py:2179-2180`` FC2,
+    ``:2465-2466`` FC1); without them a rowwise-only gather looks like a both-usage one.
+    """
+
+
+def _as_quantized(tensor: torch.Tensor, *, rowwise: bool, columnwise: bool):
+    """A stub MXFP8 tensor with exactly the usages asked for; the other slots are None.
+
+    ``rowwise=True, columnwise=False`` is what GTP's FORWARD all-gather produces
+    (``set_usage(rowwise=fwd, columnwise=not fwd)``, generalized_tensor_parallelism.py:1373), and
+    it is the shape of defect D2.
+    """
+    shadow = tensor.detach().clone().as_subclass(_StubQuantizedTensor)
+    shadow._rowwise_data = tensor.detach().clone() if rowwise else None
+    shadow._rowwise_scale_inv = torch.zeros(4) if rowwise else None
+    shadow._columnwise_data = tensor.detach().clone() if columnwise else None
+    shadow._columnwise_scale_inv = torch.ones(4) if columnwise else None
+    return shadow
+
+
+class _StubQuantizer:
+    """TE's per-weight quantizer: records what the package asks of it, returns one shadow."""
+
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        # TE's own default; an internal quantizer returns a storage with no requires_grad.
+        self.internal = True
+        self.usage: tuple | None = None
+
+    def set_usage(self, *, rowwise: bool, columnwise: bool) -> None:
+        """Record the usage demanded; columnwise is what the fused backward's wgrad reads."""
+        self.usage = (rowwise, columnwise)
+
+    def __call__(self, weight: torch.Tensor) -> "_StubQuantizedTensor":
+        """One fresh shadow per call, so a reused or aliased one is visible to the tests.
+
+        The usages honour whatever ``set_usage`` was last told, exactly as TE does: this branch
+        is asked for BOTH, which is why a BF16 expert parameter's shadow serves the dgrad and
+        needs no backward all-gather.
+        """
+        rowwise, columnwise = self.usage if self.usage is not None else (True, True)
+        return _as_quantized(weight, rowwise=rowwise, columnwise=columnwise)

+def _install_fake_transformer_engine(monkeypatch) -> list:
+    """Shadow every TransformerEngine module the expert-compute section imports lazily, and
+    return the list ``mark_not_offload`` records into."""
+    ops = ModuleType("transformer_engine.pytorch.ops")
+    ops.GroupedLinear = _StubGroupedLinear
+    ops.Sequential = _StubSequential
+    ops.ScaledSReLU = _StubScaledSReLU
+    ops.ScaledSwiGLU = _StubScaledSwiGLU
+    ops.ScaledClampedQGeGLU = _StubScaledClampedQGeGLU
+
+    grouped_mlp = ModuleType("transformer_engine.pytorch.ops.fused.grouped_mlp")
+    grouped_mlp.GroupedMLP_CuTeGEMMGLU = _StubFusedGLU
+    grouped_mlp.GroupedMLP_CuTeGEMMUnary = _StubFusedUnary
+    grouped_mlp.ScaledSReLU = _StubScaledSReLU
+    grouped_mlp._grouped_gemm_dsrelu_backward_supported = lambda: True
+    grouped_mlp._nvidia_cudnn_frontend_supports_wgrad = lambda: True
+    grouped_mlp.is_glu_activation = lambda op: isinstance(op, _StubScaledSwiGLU)
+    grouped_mlp.validate_grouped_mlp_dims = lambda fc1_op, activation_op, fc2_op: None

+    marks: list = []
+    cpu_offload = ModuleType("transformer_engine.pytorch.cpu_offload")
+    cpu_offload.mark_not_offload = marks.append
+
+    common = ModuleType("transformer_engine.pytorch.ops._common")
+    common.is_quantized_tensor = lambda tensor: isinstance(tensor, _StubQuantizedTensor)
+
+    quantization = ModuleType("transformer_engine.pytorch.quantization")
+    quantization.FP8GlobalStateManager = _StubFP8GlobalStateManager

+    pytorch = ModuleType("transformer_engine.pytorch")
+    pytorch.ops = ops

+    monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules, "transformer_engine.pytorch", pytorch)

+        ("transformer_engine.pytorch.cpu_offload", cpu_offload),
+        ("transformer_engine.pytorch.ops._common", common),
+        ("transformer_engine.pytorch.quantization", quantization),

+class TestActivationRecomputeReachesTransformerEngine:
+    """What ``'moe_act'`` in ``--recompute-modules`` does to the triple this path RUNS.
+
+    TE honours ``activation_recompute_in_mlp`` on ``ScaledSReLU`` only
+    (``grouped_mlp.py:1753-1758``). On TE 2.18 the two gated ops take the keyword and their fused
+    backward SILENTLY drops it, saving the FC2 input anyway; on te220 they raise instead
+    (``swiglu.py:473-477``) -- later, and TE's refusal rather than this package's.
+
+    The package no longer BUILDS that triple: ``TEGroupedMLP._make_fused_ops`` does and the
+    runtime borrows it. What is left to the package, and what these four pin, is the CHECK --
+    ``expert_ops`` runs ``check_fused_grouped_mlp`` over the sequence it borrowed and refuses the
+    combinations TE accepts and ignores. ACCEPTED-AND-IGNORED is invisible from the gradients,
+    which are identical either way, so a borrowed-but-unchecked sequence would be silent.
+
+    ``expert_ops`` runs for real here over a shadowed TE, which also keeps ``_DuckTypedExperts``
+    honest: every attribute the package reads off ``experts`` is resolved for real, so one
+    dropped from the stand-in is an ``AttributeError`` in this class.
+    """
+

+    def _shadow_transformer_engine(self, monkeypatch):
+        _install_fake_transformer_engine(monkeypatch)
+
+    def test_the_flag_is_carried_onto_the_op_te_honours_it_on(self):
+        """The ungated squared-ReLU triple: accepted, and cached as the ops the drain reads."""
+        runtime = _runtime_over(_DuckTypedExperts(activation_recompute=True))
+
+        sequential = runtime.expert_ops()
+
+        fc1, activation, fc2 = list(sequential.children())
+        assert (runtime._fc1_op, runtime._fc2_op) == (fc1, fc2), "the checked triple is TE's own"
+        assert sequential is runtime._experts._fused_ops[0], "borrowed, never a second shell"
+        assert isinstance(activation, _StubScaledSReLU)
+        assert activation.activation_recompute_in_mlp is True
+
+    def test_without_moe_act_the_same_triple_asks_te_for_nothing(self):
+        """The negative arm: ``activation_recompute=False`` must not set the flag at all."""
+        runtime = _runtime_over(_DuckTypedExperts(activation_recompute=False))
+
+        activation = list(runtime.expert_ops().children())[1]
+        assert activation.activation_recompute_in_mlp is False
+
+    def test_a_gated_activation_with_moe_act_is_refused(self):
+        """On 2.18 ``ScaledSwiGLU`` takes the flag and ignores it, so the package refuses first --
+        over a sequence it did not build, which is the whole of what it still owns here."""
+        runtime = _runtime_over(_DuckTypedExperts(gated=True, activation_recompute=True))

+        with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match=r"'moe_act' in recompute_modules"):

+    def test_the_same_gated_triple_is_built_when_moe_act_is_not_asked_for(self):
+        """The refusal is about the REQUEST, not the gated activation: same shape, no raise."""
+        runtime = _runtime_over(_DuckTypedExperts(gated=True, activation_recompute=False))
+
+        activation = list(runtime.expert_ops().children())[1]
+        assert isinstance(activation, _StubScaledSwiGLU)
+        assert activation.activation_recompute_in_mlp is False

+# EGTP on CPU: `expert_gtp_weight_remat_size > 1` shards every `weight{i}` on dim 0 and TE must
+# never see one -- the forward gathers once into a full-shaped shadow, the backward KEEPS it.
+
+#: Not allocator noise: generalized_tensor_parallelism.py:338-346 retains pool buffers keyed on
+#: (shape, dtype), so a recycled one holds the PREVIOUS prescaled wgrad: no `zero_()` blows up.
+_WGRAD_POOL_POISON = 7.0
+
+#: The EGTP degree the fakes shard by. 2 is enough: the shard is half the logical dim-0, which is
+#: what makes an unsharded-vs-sharded confusion a shape error rather than a silent aliasing.
+_EGTP_SIZE = 2
+
+
+class _FakeGTPWgradPool:
+    """GTP's ``_wgrad_pool_get``, with its two properties that matter kept: it is NOT zeroed, and
+    a second call hands back a DIFFERENT buffer (so a double acquire silently loses the first)."""
+
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self.handed_out: list = []
+        #: Every ``finalize_group_grads`` in call order, by leader. The ORDER is load-bearing:
+        #: the reduce-scatter is a cascade finalized by the chain PREDECESSOR's flush.
+        self.flush_order: list = []
+
+    def get(self, shape, dtype) -> torch.Tensor:
+        buffer = torch.full(tuple(shape), _WGRAD_POOL_POISON, dtype=dtype)
+        self.handed_out.append(buffer)
+        return buffer
+
+
+def _make_gtp_weight_group(
+    out_features: int, in_features: int, num_experts: int, pool: _FakeGTPWgradPool
+) -> list:
+    """One linear's EGTP group: ``num_experts`` dim-0 shards, the leader at index 0.
+
+    The five members the package touches and no more: ``is_gtp_weight_remat`` /
+    ``_unsharded_shape`` (Site 0), ``weight_list`` + ``materialize_group_for_forward`` (Site 1),
+    ``get_wgrad_tensor`` (Site 3), ``finalize_group_grads`` (Site 4). ``weight_list`` is set on
+    element 0 ONLY, as ``attach_gtp_to_presharded_module`` sets it
+    (generalized_tensor_parallelism.py:716), and every leader-only member raises on a non-leader
+    the way ``list(None)`` does at ``:1129``.
+    """
+    assert out_features % _EGTP_SIZE == 0
+    shard_rows = out_features // _EGTP_SIZE
+    weights = []
+    for index in range(num_experts):
+        weight = torch.nn.Parameter(torch.zeros((shard_rows, in_features)))
+        weight.is_gtp_weight_remat = True
+        # A real GTPShardedParam carries this, which is exactly the flag TE reads
+        # (ops/fused/grouped_mlp.py:660). The design's whole premise is that it never reaches TE.
+        weight.is_distributed_weight = True
+        weight.is_routed_expert = True
+        weight.expert_idx = index
+        weight.weight_list = None
+        weight._unsharded_shape = (out_features, in_features)
+        # Shard-shaped, as DDP sizes it: param_and_grad_buffer.py:1412-1415 is not GTP-aware.
+        weight.main_grad = torch.zeros((shard_rows, in_features))
+        # The full weight the all-gather would rebuild. Distinct per expert, so a shadow taken
+        # from the wrong index is visible rather than plausible.
+        weight._full_weight = torch.full((out_features, in_features), float(index + 1))
+        # What the BACKWARD all-gather rebuilds: the same weight COLUMNWISE, as TE's dgrad reads
+        # it. Distinct per expert AND from `_full_weight`, so a wrong graft is a wrong NUMBER.
+        weight._full_weight_bwd = _as_quantized(
+            torch.full((out_features, in_features), float(100 + index)),
+            rowwise=False,
+            columnwise=True,
+        )
+        weight._pool = pool
+        weight.materialize_calls = 0
+        weight.materialize_bwd_calls = 0
+        weight.wgrad_tensor_calls = 0
+        weight.flushes = []
+        _bind_gtp_methods(weight)
+        weights.append(weight)

+                gathered = getattr(linear, f"weight{index}")._full_weight_bwd
+                assert shadow._columnwise_data is gathered._columnwise_data
+                assert shadow._columnwise_scale_inv is gathered._columnwise_scale_inv
+                assert torch.equal(
+                    shadow._columnwise_data,
+                    torch.full_like(shadow._columnwise_data, float(100 + index)),
+                )
+
+    def test_no_forward_view_survives_the_boundary(self):
+        """THE property the whole fix rests on, and the one worth a standing test.
+
+        D1 was a held view being recycled under its holder. It cannot recur while nothing
+        gathered by the forward is still referenced once the backward starts, so assert exactly
+        that: every rowwise slot -- data and scale -- is dropped at the boundary. Read off the
+        objects the FORWARD installed, since those are the ones TE saved and therefore the ones
+        whose lifetime is in question."""
+        self._fp8_forward()
+        saved_by_the_forward = [
+            op.__dict__[f"weight{index}"] for op in self._ops for index in range(_NUM_EXPERTS)
+        ]
+
+        self.runtime.release_expert_weights()
+
+        for shadow in saved_by_the_forward:
+            assert shadow._rowwise_data is None, "a forward view survived into the backward"
+            assert shadow._rowwise_scale_inv is None
+            assert shadow._columnwise_data is not None, "and the backward view is installed"
+
+    def test_the_weight_slot_keeps_the_same_object_so_the_accumulator_lands_where_te_looks(self):
+        """The wgrad reads ``main_grad`` off the SLOT (``:659``, ``:696``) and the dgrad off the
+        forward's saved object. Re-pointing the slot at the freshly gathered tensor would split
+        the two, so the slot must still hold the object the forward saved."""
+        self._fp8_forward()
+        before = [id(shadow) for shadow in self._shadows]
+
+        self.runtime.release_expert_weights()
+
+        assert [id(shadow) for shadow in self._shadows] == before
+        for op in self._ops:
+            for index in range(_NUM_EXPERTS):
+                shadow = op.__dict__[f"weight{index}"]
+                assert shadow.main_grad is not None
+                assert tuple(shadow.main_grad.shape) == (op.out_features, op.in_features)
+
+    def test_the_backward_gathers_wrapper_is_marked_not_offloadable(self):
+        """Every chunk's fused backward saves this shadow, so an unmarked view would be
+        dequantized once per TOKEN CHUNK and free nothing."""
+        self._fp8_forward()
+        marks_before = len(self.marks)
+
+        self.runtime.release_expert_weights()
+
+        wrappers = [
+            getattr(linear, f"weight{index}")._full_weight_bwd
+            for linear in (self.seam.experts.linear_fc1, self.seam.experts.linear_fc2)
+            for index in range(_NUM_EXPERTS)
+        ]
+        newly = {id(mark) for mark in self.marks[marks_before:]}
+        assert newly == {id(wrapper) for wrapper in wrappers}
+
+    def test_the_wrappers_are_dropped_by_the_flush(self):
+        """The lifetime is exactly one layer's backward. Holding the wrappers past the flush
+        would keep GTP's gather buffer referenced across the NEXT layer's backward gather, which
+        is the two-buffer parity's one-block-ahead window and no wider."""
+        self._fp8_release()
+        for op in self._ops:
+            assert "_egtp_bwd_weight_group" in op.__dict__
+
+        self.runtime.end_wgrad_accumulation()
+
+        for op in self._ops:
+            assert "_egtp_bwd_weight_group" not in op.__dict__
+            for index in range(_NUM_EXPERTS):
+                assert f"weight{index}" not in op.__dict__
+
+    def test_the_flush_is_still_one_reduce_scatter_per_group_under_fp8_parameters(self):
+        """The added gather must not disturb the wgrad half: still ONE
+        ``finalize_group_grads`` per group per backward, on the leader, with the full list."""
+        self._fp8_release()
+
+        self.runtime.end_wgrad_accumulation()
+
+        for leader in self._leaders:
+            assert len(leader.flushes) == 1
+            assert len(leader.flushes[0]) == _NUM_EXPERTS
+
+    def test_bf16_expert_parameters_take_no_backward_gather(self):
+        """V4/N6, and the reason every previously recorded green measurement stays valid: a BF16
+        expert parameter is quantized into a FRESH both-usage tensor, which serves the dgrad, so
+        the boundary is two ``getattr`` calls and a return."""
+        self._forward()
+
+        self.runtime.release_expert_weights()
+
+        for leader in self._leaders:
+            assert leader.materialize_bwd_calls == 0, "a copy-out shadow needs no re-gather"
+        for shadow in self._shadows:
+            assert shadow._columnwise_data is not None
+            # Untouched: the copy-out branch's rowwise data is its OWN, not a view of GTP's
+            # cache, so there is nothing to drop and dropping it would break any later reader.
+            assert shadow._rowwise_data is not None
+        for op in self._ops:
+            assert "_egtp_bwd_weight_group" not in op.__dict__
+
+    def test_without_egtp_the_backward_gather_is_never_reached(self):
+        """N7: with ``expert_gtp_weight_remat_size == 1`` every line added here is unreachable,
+        not merely inert. Demonstrated by counting calls, not by reading the branch."""
+        calls = []
+        original = ep_chunk_overlap._install_backward_gather
+
+        def counting(op, weights):
+            calls.append(op)
+            return original(op, weights)
+
+        ep_chunk_overlap._install_backward_gather = counting
+        try:
+            runtime = _StubbedRuntime(_make_config(), _Seam())
+            runtime.quantize_expert_weights()
+            runtime.release_expert_weights()
+            runtime.end_wgrad_accumulation()
+        finally:
+            ep_chunk_overlap._install_backward_gather = original
+
+        assert calls == [], "the non-EGTP path must not reach the backward gather at all"
+        for op in (runtime._fc1_op, runtime._fc2_op):
+            for index in range(_NUM_EXPERTS):
+                assert f"weight{index}" not in op.__dict__
+
+
+class TestEGTPWritesNoGTPState(_EGTPFixture):
+    """The compliance property, as a test rather than as a review note.
+
+    GTP is shared code, and this package's EGTP integration is read-only against it: read one
+    flag, call the public protocol methods, never write GTP's own state. A previous revision
+    wrapped ``param._grad_accum_hook`` in place -- an attribute GTP initialises
+    (``generalized_tensor_parallelism.py:917``), sets (``:1838``) and CALLS (``:1858``) -- and
+    never restored it.
+    """
+
+    #: Attributes owned and invoked by GTP itself. Writing any of them from here replaces GTP
+    #: behaviour from outside GTP, with no file changed and nothing to restore it.
+    GTP_OWNED = (
+        "_grad_accum_hook",
+        "_grad_accum_node",
+        "_ag_ticket_fwd",
+        "_ag_ticket_bwd",
+        "_prefetch_handle",
+        "_need_weight_prefetch",
+        "_buf_parity",
+        "weight_list",
+        "chain_id",
+        "state",
+    )
+
+    def test_the_schedule_never_assigns_to_a_gtp_owned_attribute(self):
+        source = inspect.getsource(ep_chunk_overlap)
+
+        for attribute in self.GTP_OWNED:
+            for holder in ("param", "leader", "weight", "w", "shard"):
+                assert f"{holder}.{attribute} =" not in source
+                assert f"{holder}.{attribute}=" not in source
+            assert f'setattr(param, "{attribute}"' not in source
+
+    def test_the_expert_parameters_state_is_unchanged_by_a_whole_forward_and_backward(self):
+        """The behavioural half: snapshot every GTP-owned attribute the fakes carry, run the
+        real forward, boundary and flush, and require every one of them back unchanged."""
+        _make_fp8_param(self._leaders)
+        watched = [weight for leader in self._leaders for weight in leader.weight_list]
+        before = [
+            {name: id(getattr(weight, name)) for name in self.GTP_OWNED if hasattr(weight, name)}
+            for weight in watched
+        ]
+
+        self.runtime.quantize_expert_weights()
+        self.runtime.release_expert_weights()
+        self.runtime.end_wgrad_accumulation()
+
+        for weight, snapshot in zip(watched, before):
+            for name, identity in snapshot.items():
+                assert id(getattr(weight, name)) == identity, f"{name} was replaced"
+
+
+class TestEGTPHooksAreInertWithoutIt(_EGTPFixture):
+    """N1/N5: the package still imports no GTP symbol, and every added branch reads one flag."""
+
+    def test_the_schedule_touches_gtp_only_through_its_public_api(self):
+        """``gtp_api`` is the one GTP dependency allowed: it degrades to HAVE_GTP=False on a CPU-
+        only path with no TransformerEngine, so importing it costs those paths nothing. Reaching
+        past it into GTP internals would couple this schedule to a private layout instead."""
+        source = inspect.getsource(ep_chunk_overlap)
+
+        for forbidden in ("generalized_tensor_parallelism", "GTPShardedParam"):
+            assert f"import {forbidden}" not in source
+            assert f"from megatron.core.tensor_parallel.{forbidden}" not in source
+
+    def test_every_added_branch_is_gated_on_the_one_attribute(self):
+        """Read rather than imported, and the SAME attribute ``is_gtp_param`` is
+        (generalized_tensor_parallelism.py:767-769)."""
+        source = inspect.getsource(ep_chunk_overlap)
+
+        assert source.count("is_gtp_param(weights[0])") == 2
+        assert source.count("is_gtp_param(leader)") == 1
+        # The raw attribute must not be read directly: the helper is the one supported spelling.
+        assert "is_gtp_weight_remat" not in source
